item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":166,"end_unit":167,"fact_summary":"Access to specialised mental-health treatment for traumatised asylum seekers and torture survivors was highly constrained: only 4.1% of potentially needing persons could be accommodated in psychosocial support centres in 2020, with an average 7.2-month wait; in 2023 the federal government announced reducing their funding from €17.5 million to €7 million, later limiting the reduction to €4 million and providing €13.5 million for 2024.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The funding decision occurred in 2023; the access statistics are earlier but describe the conditions addressed during the period.","ruler_attribution":"The federal government announced the 2023 funding reduction; service delivery and access also depended substantially on Länder and privately operated centres.","limitations":["The source reports BAfF assessments and historical access data rather than a federal outcome evaluation.","The 2024 funding amount falls partly outside the target period."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":167,"end_unit":168,"fact_summary":"Germany lacked a systematic federal procedure for screening vulnerabilities among asylum seekers; systematic screening existed in only three Länder, protection practices varied by Land and municipality, and protection concepts were not generally legally binding or reviewed for implementation.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.3","6B.8","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report describes the institutional situation during the 2023 update, while noting that the underlying legal provision predates 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The federal legal framework required protection measures but did not create a systematic screening system; implementation was largely assigned to Länder and municipalities.","limitations":["The source does not quantify implementation across all reception centres.","The finding concerns asylum reception policy and cannot by itself establish Olaf Scholz's personal direction."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":169,"end_unit":170,"fact_summary":"By December 2023, 30,221 unaccompanied foreign children and young adults were under youth-authority care, up from 25,084 in December 2022; reception quality remained uneven, with some municipalities using regular collective accommodation or leaving young people without adequate support after age 18.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The December 2023 figure directly fits the target period; the regional-condition findings derive from earlier studies cited in the 2023 update.","ruler_attribution":"The federal government reported the national total, but accommodation and youth-welfare implementation depended mainly on Länder and local authorities.","limitations":["The source does not establish a causal effect of Scholz's decisions on the change in numbers.","The report identifies both improved conditions in some areas and continuing regional failures."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":173,"end_unit":174,"fact_summary":"Germany recorded 2,020 persons detained for removal or Dublin transfer in the first half of 2023; as of September 2023, 14 detention facilities had a combined capacity of 782 places.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","8B.3","8B.7"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The detention count and facility-capacity figures are for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Detention responsibility lay with the Länder, while the federal government supplied national parliamentary information and the federal coalition pursued return-enforcement policy.","limitations":["The 2023 detention data were incomplete because not all Länder responded and reporting practices differed.","The figures do not demonstrate conditions, legality, or personal involvement by Scholz."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":175,"end_unit":176,"fact_summary":"In 2023, Germany carried out 16,430 removals but recorded 31,770 failed removal attempts; 15,798 cancellations were attributed to local authorities revoking removal orders and 14,011 to local authorities failing to hand people over to the Federal Police, while only 295 cases cited resistance by the person being removed.","question_ids":["6B.7","8B.5","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The quantitative results cover the full 2023 calendar year.","ruler_attribution":"The federal government established the return-enforcement objective and reported the figures, but most failed-removal causes identified here occurred at local-authority level.","limitations":["A failed attempt does not necessarily mean that the person was never subsequently removed.","The source says the precise circumstances behind many local-authority cancellations were unclear."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":177,"end_unit":178,"fact_summary":"The coalition government's October 2023 Act on the Improvement of Removals proposed broadening detention and enforcement powers, including detention when grounds existed at asylum filing, extending the period in which removal could be expected from three to six months, increasing custody pending departure from 10 to 28 days, expanding searches, and reducing advance notice of removals; it also proposed providing unrepresented detainees a court-appointed lawyer and generally excluding minors and families with children from detention.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.7","3B.9","4B.2","6B.8","8B.1","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The proposal was issued in October 2023, though parliament passed it in January 2024 and it entered into force in February 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The measure was introduced by Olaf Scholz's federal coalition government; some safeguards were added during parliamentary consideration.","limitations":["Most operative legal changes occurred outside the target period.","The source records NGO criticism that the proposal expanded detention and reduced non-nationals' rights."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":179,"end_unit":180,"fact_summary":"As of 31 December 2023, asylum seekers with pending applications could generally be detained only in specified situations, including when they applied after already being detained or when they were subject to an entry ban and posed a significant security danger or had criminal convictions; NGOs criticised the latter provision as lacking safeguards for vulnerable groups and a proper EU-law basis.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.7","4B.4"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The legal situation is expressly stated as of 31 December 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The relevant detention provision had been introduced in 2020 and was administered through federal and Länder institutions; the source does not attribute its design specifically to Scholz.","limitations":["The source reports NGO legal criticism rather than a final judicial invalidation.","The provision predates the target year."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":184,"end_unit":185,"fact_summary":"German law required detention pending removal to be a last resort, limited to the shortest possible duration, and generally excluded minors and families with minors; nevertheless, lawyers and NGOs reported that detention was imposed too often and too easily, alternatives were rarely substantively considered by courts, and practices varied sharply between Länder, including detention for 96% of forced removals in Bavaria versus 17% in Lower Saxony in 2022.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.7","4B.4"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The legal safeguards applied in 2023; the comparative implementation figures are for 2022 and are used as the latest cited illustration of institutional variation.","ruler_attribution":"The federal legal framework imposed proportionality requirements, while detention decisions and use of alternatives were primarily administered by Länder authorities and courts.","limitations":["The comparative rates are not 2023 figures.","The source does not provide a nationwide 2023 rate for consideration of alternatives."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":193,"end_unit":195,"fact_summary":"In the Büren detention facility, local support groups reported that in 2023 detainees generally received only one to two hours of courtyard access per day despite a legal eight-hour standard, psychological and medical assistance was inadequate or insufficiently confidential, and three cell-fire incidents occurred; one detainee was found dead in September 2023, with the cause unknown as of March 2024.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.9","6B.2","6B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The reported courtyard access and incidents concern 2023; the source's assessment of the death remained current in March 2024.","ruler_attribution":"Büren was governed by North Rhine-Westphalia authorities; the federal government did not directly manage the facility.","limitations":["The allegations and causal interpretation are attributed to local support groups, not an official investigation.","The facility-specific evidence cannot be generalized to all German detention centres."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":196,"end_unit":197,"fact_summary":"At Pforzheim detention facility, only one of two social workers was reportedly present during the latter half of 2023, no psychological support was available, medical-care access was disputed, and a civil-society round table created in 2023 excluded staff working in the facility and the Refugee Council.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.7","6B.2","6B.4","8B.5"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The staffing and consultation findings specifically concern 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The facility was administered by Baden-Württemberg authorities; the source does not show federal direction by Scholz.","limitations":["The evidence comes primarily from Caritas and the Refugee Council rather than a federal inspection.","It is a single-facility finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":197,"end_unit":197,"fact_summary":"A November 2022 Coburg appellate decision found detention at Eichstätt unlawful because the facility's prison-like conditions did not meet the EU standard for a specialised detention facility; the Bavarian government stated that it responded by extending visiting times and allowing detainees to wear their own clothes.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The court finding predates 2023, but the reported government response remained relevant to the 2023 institutional setting.","ruler_attribution":"The decision concerned Bavarian authorities and courts, not the federal chancellor personally.","limitations":["The source does not establish whether the claimed changes fully remedied the legal deficiencies.","This is a subnational institutional finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a007cee33f0d9205","start_unit":202,"end_unit":204,"fact_summary":"German detention orders were subject to judicial review, but higher courts frequently found local detention orders unlawful; in a law firm's 2,458 represented cases through October 2023, 1,283 (52.2%) were held unlawful, with affected clients detained an average of 25.8 days. The Federal Supreme Court also issued 2023 rulings rejecting orders lacking adequate reasons, legal representation, or proportionality analysis.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.9","4B.4","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The law-firm figures extend through October 2023 and the cited Supreme Court decisions include 2023 cases.","ruler_attribution":"The evidence concerns the operation of federal detention law by local courts and authorities; it shows judicial correction but also recurring implementation failures, without establishing personal Scholz involvement.","limitations":["The law-firm sample is not a nationally representative dataset.","The source reports no comprehensive nationwide statistics on judicial-review outcomes.","Some cited case-law examples predate 2023."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied document is a Germany country report focused on asylum reception, removal, and detention; it provides little or no direct evidence on nuclear risk, international peace, macroeconomic policy, electoral competition, or personal integrity.","Most evidence concerns federal legal frameworks or Länder and local implementation, so attribution to Olaf Scholz is indirect and should not be treated as evidence of personal conduct without corroboration.","No scores are assigned."]}
